title: Maplewood Health - Redwood Onboarding Kickoff
summary: Kickoff for Maplewood Health onboarding; alignment on pilot scope (chat + embeddings), timeline (4 week pilot), security requirements (VPC, KMS, audit logs), and next steps for benchmarks, account setup, and training. AE to send contract/pricing; SE to run performance tests; CSM to schedule training and weekly check-ins.
next_steps: Miguel to run initial inference benchmark with sample payloads and share spreadsheet by 2026-07-21
Anna to send pricing deck and PO template by 2026-07-16
Priya to schedule weekly onboarding syncs starting 2026-07-20
Customer to provide sample traffic shape and redaction requirements by 2026-07-18
action_items: Miguel Torres | Run 10k token benchmark against Redwood Dedicated and Hosted variants | Due 2026-07-21
Anna Park | Share pricing, contract template, and pilot SOW | Due 2026-07-16
Priya Shah | Set up weekly onboarding cadence and invite stakeholders | Due 2026-07-17
Liam O'Connor | Provide sample prompts, embeddings use-cases, and expected QPS | Due 2026-07-18
Daniel Price | Share security checklist and KMS requirements | Due 2026-07-18
transcript: 00:00 Anna Park: hi everyone thanks for joining, we're excited to kick this off with Maplewood, can folks introduce themselves quick
00:07 Liam O'Connor: yeah hi Liam O'Connor, head of ML at Maplewood, we own the patient triage models and looking to add a chat assistant and embeddings for fast retrieval
00:14 Sara Kim: Sara here, engineering manager, i'll own integration with our backend and SSO, thanks
00:18 Daniel Price: Daniel - security and compliance, i'll be focused on encryption, audit logs, and data residency
00:24 Anna Park: great, i'll run through agenda then miguel will cover technical runbook and priya on onboarding timeline
01:05 Anna Park: agenda is: intros, success criteria, infra options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), security requirements, pilot scope, and next steps

02:10 Miguel Torres: quick note on variants - Redwood Hosted gives fastest time to value, Dedicated gives reserved capacity and predictable throughput, Private is for VPC/onprem needs, we've seen customers start hosted then move to dedicated if they need throughput guarantees
03:02 Liam O'Connor: our main constrains are latency < 300ms p50 for chat, cost targets per 1k messages, and we need data not to leave our VPC for the PII paths
03:28 Miguel Torres: noted, we can route PII-containing requests to Dedicated or Private with KMS integration, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS and HSM for key control
04:00 Daniel Price: can you confirm SOC2 and audit logs? we need an attestation and detailed logging for model inference calls
04:15 Miguel Torres: yes we provide audit logs in the Console and for Private we can push logs to customer's SIEM, SOC2 report available in our security pack, i'll attach that doc
05:12 Sara Kim: integration surface - what SDKs and patterns do you recommend for streaming chat?

05:25 Miguel Torres: we have REST SDKs and real-time streaming websocket patterns, we recommend streaming with chunked responses for UX; also prefix caching / KV cache can improve latency on repeated prompts (sometimes transcribed as K V cash in old notes)
06:40 Liam O'Connor: about benchmarking - we have variable input sizes, can SE run sample run across both quantized and fp16 models?
06:58 Miguel Torres: yes we'll run tests across a couple model variants, quantized 4-bit vs float16, measure p50/p95 and token cost; we'll also check cold start w/ empty KV cache and warmed cache
08:10 Anna Park: pilot scope proposal - 4 weeks, deliverables: production-like benchmark, integration guide, security review, and a training session for devs
08:25 Priya Shah: onboarding timeline - week1: account setup and access, week2: benchmarks and proof, week3: integration work and custom prompts, week4: training and handover
09:50 Daniel Price: on network topology - for Private deployment, do you support VPC peering or private endpoints?
10:05 Miguel Torres: yes both; for hosted we have private endpoints and customer can set up VPC egress rules, for Private we deploy into customer VPC or on-prem containerized package
11:30 Sara Kim: any gotchas with rate limits or burst handling? we expect traffic spikes from evening triage windows
11:45 Miguel Torres: we recommend autoscaling policies with burst capacity on Dedicated; also intelligent batching helps reduce unit cost but introduces headroom trade-offs
12:55 Liam O'Connor: curious about model rollouts and A/B test support
13:05 Miguel Torres: Console supports rollout policies, canary, A/B, automatic fallback to compatible model variants, and per-route monitoring for latency and cost
14:20 Daniel Price: will need to review data retention and redaction options; do you offer automatic PII redaction at inference time?

14:35 Miguel Torres: we have integrations and patterns for client-side redaction; server-side we can offer masking rules and can route sensitive traffic to Private where logs are controlled, i'll include patterns
16:00 Anna Park: for budget and contracting - we expect a pilot invoice and then potential reserved capacity if numbers look good; i'll send a draft SOW and pricing
16:20 Liam O'Connor: our procurement cycle is about 3 weeks post-pilot if approvals go smoothly
18:00 Priya Shah: training - we can do a 60-90 minute dev workshop and a separate ops runbook session, which would you prefer first?
18:12 Sara Kim: dev workshop first is ideal
20:05 Miguel Torres: i'll start running the initial benchmark after we get sample payloads; please send a few representative prompts and embedding queries
21:30 Anna Park: to recap next steps: miguel benchmarks, anna pricing and SOW, priya schedule weekly syncs, maples to share samples and security checklist
22:00 Daniel Price: noted, i'll share the security checklist and KMS requirements by end of week
23:10 Liam O'Connor: thanks everyone, excited to get started
23:15 Anna Park: thanks all, we'll follow up with notes and links - action items in the CRM and i'll create the pilot ticket
